kernels.kernel_name: fused_conv_relu_pool_kernel(const __half *, __half *, int, int, int, int, int, int)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090 (Blackwell, sm_120). Lots of SMs, huge HBM/GDDR7 BW, ample shared memory. fp16 with fast math. Tensor cores available for half MMA.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Conv 3x3 16->32, H=720, W=1280, N=1. Output of pool is 32x360x640. Pure compute is tiny vs memory traffic; problem is memory-bandwidth bound.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input: 1*16*720*1280*2B = ~29.5MB. Output (post-pool): 1*32*360*640*2B = ~14.7MB. Conv intermediate (if not fused): ~58.9MB. Fusing conv+relu+pool eliminates intermediate.

register_pressure.notes: Weights total: 32*16*3*3*2B = 9216B (~9KB) — fits easily in shared memory or even registers across a block. Bias: 32*2B = 64B.

nodes.notes:
ANALYSIS:
1) Classification: stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + 2x2 reduction (avgpool). Dense NCHW fp16. Small fixed Cin=16, Cout=32; large H=720, W=1280; N=1.
2) Math: out[co,oh,ow] = avg over 2x2 of ReLU(bias[co] + sum_ci sum_kh sum_kw in[ci,2oh+kh-1+dy,2ow+kw-1+dx]*W[co,ci,kh,kw]). Reductions across ci(16) and 3x3 and 2x2. All can be fused per output element.
3) Layout: input NCHW contiguous fp16, weights tiny (9KB fits in shared/registers). Output (post-pool) 32*360*640. Each input pixel is read by up to 9 conv outputs and combined into pool. Reuse along H/W is high.
4) Regimes: (a) full fusion conv+relu+pool: bandwidth-bound by input read + output write (~44MB). (b) Separate conv kernel: emits 58MB intermediate, doubles traffic. (c) Tensor-core path: Cin=16, Cout=32 — fits a single MMA shape (m16n8k16). 3x3 conv as 9 GEMMs or im2col-free direct.
5) Knobs: fuse all 3 ops, weights in shared/constant, tile over (oh,ow) with halo, vectorize via __half2 / float4 loads, use tensor cores for Cin*9=144 reduction per output pixel, output 2x2 tiles per thread for pool fusion.
6) Skeleton: block tiles a region of pool-output (e.g., 16x32 pool outputs => 32x64 conv outputs => need 34x66 input halo). Load input tile into shared mem, weights into shared/constant, each thread computes a small set of conv outputs across all Cout, applies ReLU, pools in-register, writes pool output.
7) Families: (F1) Fully-fused stencil tile kernel with shared-mem input tile and weights in shared/constant — TOP. (F2) Tensor-core (WMMA) fused conv+relu+pool treating channels as MMA-K dim. (F3) Two-pass: optimized conv+relu producing intermediate, then fast pool — fallback.
Key constraints: rtol/atol 0.01 (loose, fp16 accum OK with fp32 partials). RTX5090 sm120.

action.description: Implement a single fused CUDA kernel that performs Conv3x3+bias+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 in one pass. Tile output across (oh,ow); each block loads an input halo tile into shared memory; weights kept in shared memory or constant memory; each thread computes a 2x2 conv patch for one or more Cout channels, applies ReLU, averages, writes one pool output. Use fp32 accumulators. Eliminates the 58MB intermediate write/read.
action.rationale: Removes a full intermediate tensor pass; weights are tiny and fit in shared memory; tile reuse amortizes halo loads. Should be bandwidth-optimal.
action.title: F1: Fused conv+relu+avgpool single kernel with shared-mem input tile

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Plenty of shared memory on sm120. Tile size limited by smem (e.g., 32x64 conv output -> 34x66 halo per Cin channel = 34*66*16*2B = ~72KB; may need smaller tiles or per-channel streaming).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute throughput 83.4% — excellent. Tensor cores unused (0%). FP16 loads converted to FP32 MAC.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Achieved BW only 51 GB/s and mem throughput 8.9% — kernel is compute/latency bound, not BW bound. Halo reuse working well.

register_pressure.notes: 64 regs/thread with launch_bounds(128,8); acc[8][4]=32 floats per thread. Could be reduced via warp-level cooperation but currently OK with 64.46% occupancy.

nodes.notes: CURRENT: does=fused Conv3x3+bias+ReLU+AvgPool2x2 in one kernel; each block produces an 8x16 output tile across 8 output channels, halo-loaded into shared mem, weights in constant mem; each thread computes a 2x2 conv patch then pools. bottleneck=compute/latency (compute_throughput 83%, mem 9%). FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent=yes. UPDATE_BELIEF: eval shows 7.31x speedup vs ref (0.698ms vs 5.10ms), well above the 3x prior. Bandwidth is NOT the bottleneck; achieved BW only 51 GB/s. next bet: push further via (a) vectorized __half2 loads + FMA on half2 to halve issue count, (b) bigger CO_PER_BLOCK / output-channel reuse to amortize shared-mem reads, or (c) tensor-core WMMA path. PERF_GAP: expected 3.0x, observed 7.31x — underestimated; halo reuse + constant-mem weights + compute overlap stronger than predicted.

action.description: Use WMMA / mma.sync tensor cores treating (Cin*9)=144 as K dimension and Cout=32 as N. Materialize a small im2col-like operand fragment per output tile or pack 9 channel-shifted views. Fuse ReLU and 2x2 pool on the output fragments in registers before writing.
action.rationale: Tensor cores give a big throughput edge; Cout=32 maps well to m16n16. However problem is bandwidth-bound, so TC may not help dramatically beyond F1.
action.title: F2: Tensor-core fused conv+relu+pool

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: WMMA m16n16k16 fp16 fits Cout=32 (two N tiles). Channel dim 16 fits K=16 exactly; would need 9 K-iterations for spatial taps.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: TC util only 7.5% - underutilized; K=144 small, lots of overhead from im2col build.

memory_bandwidth.notes: BW only 52.7 GB/s; problem is BW-bound, TC doesn't help.

nodes.notes:
CURRENT: does: WMMA-based fused conv(3x3)+ReLU+avgpool2x2 using im2col into shared memory, K=144, N=32, M=32 per block (2 warps). bottleneck: shared-memory build of im2col (sA fill = 4608 halfs/block) plus only 7.5% TC utilization — too small a problem for TC to amortize im2col cost.
FOLLOW_THROUGH: aligned_with_intent: yes. WMMA fused kernel implemented with bias+ReLU+pool fused.
UPDATE_BELIEF: TC path measured 6.95x (lat 0.648ms) — WORSE than fused vec n_fused_vec at 9.17x (0.454ms). The im2col materialization and small per-block work overwhelm TC benefit; tensor_core_utilization only 7.5%, occupancy 32.65%, smem 11136B. next bet: abandon TC for this shape; continue improving n_fused_vec via vectorized half2 IO, async cp.async pipelined halo loads, and larger output tiles. PERF_GAP: expected_vs_baseline=11.0 vs observed speedup=6.95x — gap due to high im2col cost and low TC occupancy at this small Cin/Cout.

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2d(3x3, pad=1, 16->32) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2x2) on fp16 NCHW input of shape (1,16,720,1280) producing (1,32,360,640). Weights are tiny (~9KB) and fit comfortably in shared/constant memory; the workload is memory-bandwidth bound, so the dominant optimization is to fuse all three ops into a single kernel and eliminate the ~58MB conv intermediate. Stencil reuse across the 3x3 window favors shared-memory input tiling with halos. Tolerance is loose (rtol/atol=0.01) so fp32 accumulation with fp16 storage is safe. Target: RTX5090 (sm_120), CUDA, fp16.
open_questions: What is the reference kernel's measured latency on RTX5090 — is conv or pool the dominant cost?
What shared-memory tile size best balances halo overhead vs occupancy on sm120 (e.g., 32x64 vs 16x32 pool-output tiles)?
Are weights best placed in __constant__ memory (broadcast-friendly) or shared memory (more flexible indexing)?
Does loading the entire 16-channel halo tile at once exceed smem budget for desired occupancy, or should Cin be streamed/looped?
Will vectorized half2/uint4 loads be alignment-safe given W=1280 (multiple of 8) and padding logic?
Is tensor-core utilization worth the complexity if the kernel is bandwidth-bound?
Does N=1 limit parallelism enough that we need to tile aggressively across (oh,ow) and Cout to fill SMs?
Are there any non-contiguous strides we must handle, or can we assume contiguous NCHW after the .contiguous() call?
